clue.text: Pillager's trick divides his confederates.

definitions.note: the possessive is read as 'Pillager is', so the definition is the noun alone

indicators.note: one thing that divides another sits inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: a band is a group of confederates or accomplices
to rig is to fix or trick, as with a rigged game

explanation.surface: A looter's scheme causes a rift among his partners in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divides' puts RIG inside BAND, splitting it as B-RIG-AND; the apostrophe-S on 'Pillager's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit who robs and plunders, which is exactly what a pillager does.

clue.text: Worker supports the beadle, giving him a buzz?

definitions.text: Worker supports the beadle, giving him a buzz?

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: Mr Bumble is the beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist
a worker bee is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee props up a parish official and cheers him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' places BEE beneath BUMBLE in the down grid. The whole clue paints the insect: a worker that buzzes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumblebee is a large hairy bee with a loud hum, buzzing as it flies.

clue.text: Give rise to a popular feature of church architecture

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Inspire a well-loved element of ecclesiastical design.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to prompt or bring about, to be the cause of something.

clue.text: Extraordinarily, cheap tyre-a typical example

indicators.note: extraordinarily means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually cheap tyre, the standard model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' rearranges CHEAP TYRE. The page has a dash before 'a typical example', misread by the OCR as '-a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is a perfect specimen or model of its kind.

clue.text: 'A stupid sort to take part in fitness training!

parts.note: to do is to perform, take part
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Only a fool would take part in fitness classes.
explanation.walkthrough: PE, physical education, is what British schools call gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a slow-witted person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Reserve fund obtains backing in north, say

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: backing means the word for obtains is read from right to left

parts.note: to obtain something is to get it, so gets

explanation.surface: Money set aside earns interest back home in the north, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for obtains; the surface's 'backing' suggests financial support, apt for a fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money saved up for the future, a financial reserve.

clue.text: Zoology student in Berlin is subnormal

parts.note: a natural was once a term for a person of low intelligence
ist is German for is, as spoken in Berlin

explanation.surface: A zoology student in the German capital is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Berlin' signals a German word; 'subnormal' uses the old sense of natural as a simpleton, not 'normal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalist studies plants and animals, including zoology.

clue.text: The Slippery Slope" — an endless harangue

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a screed is a long harangue or rant

explanation.surface: A book title, perhaps, for a long rant that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of SCREED. The quotation marks pretend it is a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is loose stony debris on a hillside, which slides underfoot.

clue.text: A girl caught one after church, burrowing and laying eggs

indicators.note: something caught is held inside

parts.note: Edna is a girl's name

indicators.note: one piece after another comes next in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl grabs someone after church services, digging and laying eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is the container signal, not the cricket abbreviation C; 'after' orders church before one. The definition describes the creature's habits.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater is an egg-laying mammal that digs burrows.

clue.text: Lame writer accepting medal

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: John Gay was an English writer, author of The Beggar's Opera
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A writer with a bad leg gets a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal. Gammy is British slang for a bad leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammy is informal British for injured or crippled, describing a bad leg.

clue.text: Notes thus written by an Athenian: character

indicators.note: one piece written by another sits beside it, here following it

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character an Athenian would write
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written

explanation.surface: Musical notes set down by an ancient Greek, thus, as a sort of letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'an Athenian character'; the colon is an OCR artefact. 'written by' puts the Latin word after the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes on a stave are written music; a collection of notes is what a musician plays from.

clue.text: Give out: ersatz: fabric

parts.note: to peter out is to dwindle or give out, so peter alone means give out
something ersatz is fake, a sham

explanation.surface: Run out of the real thing and make do with a fake cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon or heavy woollen cloth used for belts and overcoats.

clue.text: Hang about and see the king swallow drink

indicators.note: one piece swallowing another takes it inside, like a mouth around food

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
ER is a royal cipher, standing for a king or queen as Rex or Regina
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Linger and watch the monarch down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' is the container signal around the joined first two pieces. It is Italian vermouth, as in the British pub order gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, waiting about with no purpose.

clue.text: Intimate as learned barristers can be?

explanation.surface: Close friends, as lawyers in court sometimes are.
explanation.walkthrough: British barristers address each other in court as 'my learned friend', hence the second, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate means close and warm; barristers' courtroom formula 'my learned friend' makes them at least nominally so.

clue.text: Potential customers, carrying University brochure

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

parts.note: prospects are potential customers

explanation.surface: Possible buyers have the university's information leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts U inside PROSPECTS, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a booklet describing a school, university or company offering.

clue.text: Neat description of a muscular fellow

definitions.text: Neat description of a muscular fellow

parts.words: Neat description of a muscular fellow
parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a description of neat is an adjective from their meat, which also describes a brawny man

explanation.surface: A tidy way to sum up a strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy', but it is the old word for oxen and cattle; the adjective drawn from their meat also fits a hefty man.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means brawny and well built, like an ox or a strong man.

clue.text: Unwilling to make cattle run amok

indicators.note: running amok means rushing about wildly, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Not keen to cause a stampede among the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run amok' shuffles the letters of CATTLE RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant describes someone who is not keen and holds back from doing something.

clue.text: Players holding a practice session — they're in the kitchen

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside

parts.note: casts are the players in shows
in cricket, a net is a practice session

explanation.surface: Actors take part in a practice, and then go to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal. 'Kitchen' is slang for an orchestra's percussion section, not the room for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are hand-held clappers played in the percussion section, nicknamed the kitchen.

clue.text: Go trip the fantastic? Not on this, surely!

definitions.text: Go trip the fantastic? Not on this, surely!

indicators.note: fantastic means wild and fanciful, so the letters are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer is told not to trip the light fantastic on a high wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges GO TRIP THE, echoing 'trip the light fantastic', to dance; the whole clue then says no one should try dancing on this.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a high wire stretched for acrobats, where any trip would be a fall.

clue.text: Refreshments supplied otherwise by son outside flat

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps around it

parts.note: else means otherwise, as in 'or else'
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Snacks handed out in another way by a boy standing outside an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal. Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light snack with tea or coffee in the mid-morning, a break for refreshments.

clue.text: Some long-forgotten gag editors once commissioned

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Editors of old jokes who were long ago taken on.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means hired or taken on, an old sense of commissioning someone.

clue.text: Young man bound .to .lose knight in game.

indicators.note: to lose a letter is to drop it from the word

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
in chess notation the knight is N

explanation.surface: A lad is sure to give up his knight in a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes N from SPRING. 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprig is an old, slightly dismissive word for a youth or young man.

clue.text: He wrote rhymes at first about a gemstone

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of the word before

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
sard is a reddish-brown gemstone

explanation.surface: He wrote rhymes about a jewel to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: RONSARD was a French Renaissance poet. 'about' is ON, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The French poet was a sixteenth-century writer of sonnets and odes.

clue.text: Nickname for one commanding FBI agents without number

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: G-men are government men, US slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: A nickname for the man in charge of federal agents who lack a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so it wraps rather than removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a surname or an extra name given to someone, an epithet or byname.

clue.text: This sounds like the colonel's lady, soft-hearted

annotationWithheld.why: This sounds like the colonel's lady, soft-hearted (5): wordplay is P (soft) inside CORA (Colonel Munro's daughter), but no word fairly defines coconut kernel and 'sounds like' fits nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: This sounds like the colonel's lady, soft-hearted

clue.text: Hold forth — alternatively a note must be written

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Lecture, or else a note needs to be written.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously, deliver a speech.

clue.text: Girl swallowed by great sea-bird

indicators.note: a thing swallowed by another ends up inside it

parts.note: GT is an abbreviation for great
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is gulped down by a huge seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts ANNE inside GT, the abbreviation for great.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannets are large white seabirds that dive for fish, known for their appetite.

clue.text: Stainer is terrible, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A painter is awful, according to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stainer' looks like John Stainer the composer, but means one who stains cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours fabric, staining it with dye.

clue.text: Future knight has an attempt at pompous spectacle

parts.note: in medieval times a page was a boy in training to become a knight
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A squire in waiting makes a stab at grand ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A page served in a noble household before becoming a squire and then a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate display and ceremony, a showy spectacle.

clue.text: A daughter of Zeus displaced 23

indicators.note: displaced letters are moved out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the number points to the answer of 23 down, a word meaning hold forth

explanation.surface: One of the god's daughters has been moved from her place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges the letters of the answer to 23 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were daughters of Zeus; this one presides over love poetry.

clue.text: Apply oneself to'making a speech

explanation.surface: Get down to the business of speaking in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'to making'; the apostrophe is an OCR artefact. To address oneself to a task is to apply oneself to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a task is to tackle it; an address is also a formal talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: The rest are upper-class and live … outside

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps around it

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: The others are posh and dwell out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts RESIDE around U, giving RESID-U-E. U is the British label for upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder.
